Wayne County Friend of the Court

Address: Penobscot Building, 645 Griswold St, Detroit, MI 48226, United States

Phone: +18447857593

If you are a resident of Wayne County, Michigan, and are involved in a family law case, you may have heard of the Wayne County Friend of the Court (WCFOC). But what exactly is the Wayne County Friend of the Court, and what services does it provide? In this article, we will provide a comprehensive overview of the Wayne County Friend of the Court, including its history, services offered, and how to file a case.

What is Wayne County Friend of the Court?

The Wayne County Friend of the Court is a state-funded organization that provides support to families involved in family law cases in Wayne County, Michigan. The organization was established in the 1930s to assist the courts in enforcing court orders and resolving family law issues.

The WCFOC provides a variety of services to families, including child support enforcement, parenting time enforcement, and mediation services. These services are designed to help families resolve disputes and ensure that court orders are followed.

Services offered by Wayne County Friend of the Court

Child support enforcement

The WCFOC provides child support enforcement services to families in Wayne County. This includes collecting child support payments and distributing them to the custodial parent. If a non-custodial parent fails to make child support payments, the WCFOC may take enforcement actions, such as wage garnishment or seizure of assets.

Parenting time enforcement

The WCFOC also provides parenting time enforcement services. This means that the organization can assist in enforcing court-ordered parenting time schedules. If a parent fails to comply with a parenting time schedule , the WCFOC may take enforcement actions, such as contempt of court proceedings or modification of the parenting time schedule.

Mediation services

In addition to child support enforcement and parenting time enforcement, the WCFOC also offers mediation services. Mediation is a process where a neutral third party helps families resolve disputes. The WCFOC provides mediation services to families in Wayne County to help them resolve disputes related to child support, parenting time, and other family law issues.

How to file a case with Wayne County Friend of the Court

If you are involved in a family law case in Wayne County, you may need to file a case with the WCFOC. The following are the requirements for filing a case and the steps you need to take:

  1. Requirements: You must be a resident of Wayne County and have a pending family law case in the county to file a case with the WCFOC.
  2. Steps:
    • Contact the WCFOC to request a case review.
    • Provide the WCFOC with the necessary information and documents related to your case.
    • Attend a case review meeting with the WCFOC to discuss the details of your case.
    • Follow the recommendations and instructions provided by the WCFOC.

Modifying a child support order

There may come a time when you need to modify a child support order. The following are some reasons why you may need to modify a child support order and the steps you need to take:

  1. Reasons: You may need to modify a child support order if there has been a significant change in circumstances, such as a change in income or living situation.
  2. Steps:
    • Contact the WCFOC to request a modification of the child support order.
    • Provide the WCFOC with the necessary information and documents related to the change in circumstances.
    • Attend a hearing to present your case and the evidence supporting the modification.
    • Follow the instructions provided by the court and the WCFOC.

Parenting time enforcement

If you are having trouble enforcing a parenting time schedule, the WCFOC can help. The following are the steps you need to take to enforce a parenting time order:

  1. Steps:
    • Contact the WCFOC to request enforcement of the parenting time order.
    • Provide the WCFOC with the necessary information and documents related to the parenting time schedule.
    • Attend a hearing to present your case and the evidence supporting the enforcement.
    • Follow the instructions provided by the court and the WCFOC.

Mediation services

If you are in a dispute with the other parent related to child support, parenting time, or other family law issues, the WCFOC can help. The following are the steps you need to take to use the WCFOC's mediation services:

  1. Steps:
    • Contact the WCFOC to request mediation services.
    • Attend a mediation session with the other parent and the mediator.
    • Discuss the dispute and work with the mediator to reach a resolution.
    • Follow the agreement reached during the mediation session.

Payment options for child support

If you are a non-custodial parent and need to make child support payments, the WCFOC offers several payment options. The following are the payment options available:

  1. Online payment: You can make child support payments online through the WCFOC's website.
  2. Automated phone system: You can make child support payments over the phone using the WCFOC's automated phone system.
  3. In-person payment: You can make child support payments in person at the WCFOC's office.
  4. Mail payment: You can mail a check or money order to the WCFOC's office.

Regardless of the payment option you choose, it is important to keep track of your payments and make sure they are received by the WCFOC on time.

Contacting Wayne County Friend of the Court

If you need to contact the WCFOC, you can do so by phone or email. The following is the contact information for the WCFOC:

Phone: (313) 224-5300 Email: friendofthecourt@waynecounty.com

The WCFOC's office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM.

Wayne County Family Court Case Lookup

If you want to look up information about a family law case in Wayne County, you can do so online. The Wayne County Clerk's Office provides an online case search tool that allows you to search for cases by case number, party name, or attorney name. This tool can be accessed on the Wayne County Clerk's Office website.

Wayne County Friend of the Court Online

The Wayne County Friend of the Court provides several online services to families involved in family law cases in Wayne County. These services include online child support payment options, online case information, and online forms. To access these services, you can visit the Wayne County Friend of the Court website.

Conclusion

The Wayne County Friend of the Court is a valuable resource for families involved in family law cases in Wayne County, Michigan. With its child support enforcement, parenting time enforcement, and mediation services, the WCFOC helps families resolve disputes and ensure that court orders are followed. If you are involved in a family law case in Wayne County, we encourage you to learn more about the WCFOC and the services it provides.
